documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Outside gynecology, visit 01/11/2022. Six weeks after uterine artery embolization (11/30/2021). ED visit two days post procedure for post-embolization syndrome, settled with NSAIDs. First period since was noticeably lighter, about four days, no clots, did not miss work. Abdomen soft, nontender. Plan: no further intervention; will reassess if bleeding returns. Back to routine gynecologic care with PCP. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 43F. Feeling well. Energy good since spironolactone. Periods lighter since the embolization in Nov. No headaches beyond the odd one from grading late. Home BP mostly 128-136 / 80s.
Meds: spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, levothyroxine 125, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Social: teaching 2nd grade at the new school, likes it. Walks after work. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Family: mother breast ca at 58; father HTN and cerebral aneurysm; sister hypothyroid.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. Thyroidectomy scar healed. Breasts symmetric, no masses, no nipple change, axillae clear. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin unremarkable.
A/P
- Primary aldosteronism / resistant HTN: at goal-ish at home. CMP today for K and Cr.
- PTC s/p thyroidectomy: endo yearly, TSH today.
- Fibroids s/p UAE: improved.
- Screening: Tdap today. HCV and HIV screening today. Cervical co-test due 2025. Mammogram - mother's history; she's had one in 2020, order screening yearly - she'd like to wait until summer when school is out.
- Flu given in the fall; COVID booster discussed.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH normal. K normal on spironolactone + lisinopril. HCV and HIV nonreactive. Portal message sent.

conditions.label: Lump in right breast, upper outer quadrant

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - breast lump
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Found a lump in her right breast in the shower about a month ago. Has not changed since. Not painful. No discharge from the nipple, no skin dimpling or redness. She has been checking it every day and admits she is scared - mother's cancer, plus her own thyroid cancer last year. Sleeping less. GAD-7 8.
Exam: firm mass about 1.5 cm R breast upper outer quadrant, does not move freely, nontender. No skin changes, no nipple retraction. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. L breast normal.
A/P
1. Palpable R breast mass. Diagnostic mammogram + targeted ultrasound, marked urgent. Explained most lumps at her age turn out benign but this one needs imaging and likely a biopsy.
2. Situational anxiety around the lump. Talked it through; she'd rather not start anything, has her sister for support. Will move quickly so she's not waiting. Message me anytime.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with spot compression of the right breast. Breasts heterogeneously dense. A BB marker at the palpable site, right breast upper outer quadrant, overlies an oval circumscribed equal-density mass. No suspicious calcifications. Left breast: no mass, distortion or suspicious calcifications.
reports.conclusion: Oval circumscribed mass at the palpable site, right breast. See ultrasound.

reports.text: Targeted right breast ultrasound at the palpable site. At 10 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple: oval, circumscribed, hypoechoic solid mass, parallel orientation, 1.6 x 1.0 x 1.2 cm. No posterior shadowing. Right axilla: normal lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 1.6 cm solid mass, right breast 10 o'clock, corresponding to the palpable finding. BI-RADS 4A: low suspicion for malignancy. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy recommended.

reports.text:
Specimen: right breast, 10 o'clock, ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (4 cores).

documents.title: Breast biopsy report
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside breast imaging center. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy, right breast 10 o'clock, 14-gauge, 4 cores, 06/28/2022. Clip placed, confirmed on post-procedure mammogram. No complications.
Addendum 07/01: pathology fibroadenoma, benign and concordant with imaging. Recommend follow-up right breast ultrasound in 6 months, then annual screening mammography.

documents.title: Biopsy result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called with path: fibroadenoma, benign. She cried with relief. Follow-up ultrasound in 6 months per radiology, then yearly mammograms. Ordered.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, visit 09/13/2022.
One year after total thyroidectomy for 2.5 cm PTC (vascular invasion, N0), no RAI. Feels well. Benign breast biopsy this summer.
Levothyroxine 125 mcg; TSH in range today. Thyroglobulin <0.1. Neck ultrasound 09/08: empty thyroid bed, no abnormal nodes.
Excellent response to therapy. Continue current dose; yearly TSH, thyroglobulin and ultrasound.
Aldosteronism: on spironolactone 50 with lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ. K and creatinine normal today. BP 134/84 here. Continue. Return 1 year.

orders.reason: progressive headaches with nocturnal and positional features, morning vomiting

documents.title: Office Visit - headaches
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Headaches since late summer, close to three months. Dull, all over the front, worse at night and when she bends to help the kids at their desks. Some mornings nauseated and has vomited a few times before work. Acetaminophen takes the edge off. Never had headaches like this.
BP fine at home. No fever, no trauma.
Exam: BP normal. Alert, fluent. Cranial nerves grossly intact. Moves all limbs; gait normal.
A/P: new progressive headache with nighttime/positional worsening and morning vomiting - red flags. Urgent neurology referral today for evaluation and brain imaging; called the neurology office myself to get her in. ED if sudden severe headache, weakness, vision change or confusion. Acetaminophen as needed in the meantime.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily, then taper over 4 weeks as directed

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, visit 12/12/2022. Urgent referral from PCP.
44F with primary aldosteronism and papillary thyroid carcinoma treated by thyroidectomy in 2021. Three months of dull aching headache, worse at night and on bending forward, with nausea and some morning vomiting.
Meds: spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, levothyroxine, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: BP normal. Mild left-sided weakness, 4+/5 arm and leg. Slight tremor of the left hand. Rest of the neuro exam normal.
MRI brain with and without contrast (same day): 2 cm enhancing right frontal lobe mass with vasogenic edema.
Impression: right frontal brain mass with edema explaining her headache and left-sided signs.
Plan: dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily, tapering over 4 weeks. Urgent neurosurgery referral placed. No driving until neurosurgery has seen her. Return for worse headache, vomiting, weakness or seizure.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home. Neurology letter and MRI reviewed with her: 2 cm right frontal mass with edema. On dexamethasone a week - headache much better, no vomiting since Wednesday, says the left hand feels steadier. Some trouble sleeping on the steroid. Neurosurgery appt Jan 10.
Taking the week off before break; colleagues covering. Mother staying with her.
A/P: R frontal mass - added to list. Steroid: take with food, take the dose by early afternoon. Watch BP and sugars while on it - no symptoms of high sugar. Let me know what neurosurgery says. ED precautions reviewed.

reports.text: Right breast 10 o'clock: biopsy-proven fibroadenoma, oval circumscribed hypoechoic mass, 1.6 x 1.0 x 1.1 cm, unchanged. Biopsy clip in place.
reports.conclusion: Stable biopsy-proven fibroadenoma. BI-RADS 2: benign. Return to annual screening mammography.

documents.title: Neurosurgery consultation
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Outside neurosurgery, visit 01/10/2023.
44F referred by neurology for a 2 cm enhancing right frontal mass with vasogenic edema (MRI 12/12/2022), found on workup of three months of headache with mild left-sided weakness and left-hand tremor. On a dexamethasone taper; headache gone, weakness and tremor resolved.
PMH: primary aldosteronism; papillary thyroid cancer, thyroidectomy 2021, no evidence of disease.
Exam today: neuro intact, strength 5/5 throughout, no tremor.
Imaging reviewed: the appearance favors a meningioma.
Discussion: offered resection now versus surveillance MRI now that she is asymptomatic. She wishes to avoid surgery if she can and to finish the school year. Reasonable. Repeat MRI in 3 months; sooner for any recurrent headache, weakness or seizure. Finish the steroid taper. OK to drive.

documents.body:
Annual. 44F. Off dexamethasone since mid-January, no headaches. Neurosurgery watching the R frontal mass, repeat MRI in April. Back at work fully. Worry about the mass comes and goes; sleeping better. GAD-7 4.
Meds: spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, levothyroxine 125, acetaminophen PRN.
Exam: well appearing. Neuro: strength symmetric, no tremor, gait normal. Breasts: small firm mobile R UOQ lump at the biopsy site, unchanged; no other masses. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abd benign, no edema.
A/P
- R frontal mass, likely meningioma per neurosurgery: on surveillance.
- Aldosteronism/HTN: stable, CMP today.
- Hx PTC: endo yearly.
- Fibroadenoma R breast: stable on Jan US. Screening mammogram this summer.
- Colorectal screening at 45 - next year.
Labs today.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 12/14/2023.
CC: severe headaches, morning nausea, blurry vision.
HPI: 45F with a known right frontal mass on surveillance and primary aldosteronism. Over recent weeks her headaches have become severe and throbbing, felt at the back of the head, daily and worst on waking, with nausea and vomiting most mornings. Brief episodes of blurred vision. No head injury, no new medications.
Meds: spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, levothyroxine, acetaminophen. NKDA.
Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 78. BMI 30.
Exam: bilateral papilledema on fundoscopy. Remainder of neurologic exam unremarkable.
MRI brain: known right frontal mass, now with more surrounding edema.
ED diagnosis: structural intracranial lesion with raised pressure signs.
Course: dexamethasone 10 mg IV. Headache improved. Discussed with on-call neurosurgery, who know her - plan resection; to be scheduled within weeks.
Dispo: home on dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily until surgery. Return for worsening headache, vomiting, vision loss, weakness or seizure.

documents.title: Post-ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED last Thursday - several weeks of worsening morning headaches with vomiting and blurred vision; papilledema; MRI known R frontal mass with more edema. Back on dexamethasone 4 bid. Neurosurgery booked craniotomy Jan 9.
Today: headaches much less, no vomiting since steroid. Vision clear. Nervous about surgery but says it's a relief to have a plan. On leave from school until after recovery.
Exam: alert, neuro nonfocal, strength 5/5.
A/P: R frontal mass - surgery 1/9. Steroid precautions as before. Pre-op labs will be done by neurosurgery. Will see her after.
